newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Six missing children walk out of Australian outback.
newsitem.headline: Six missing children walk out of Australian outback.

text.p: A group of 13 missing children, including an infant, were safe and well on Monday after six of them walked out of the remote Australian outback to end a two-day search, police said.

The group, led by an Aboriginal woman, had gone missing on Saturday while out gathering native grubs near the gold mining town of Norseman, 550 km (340 miles) east of Perth in Western Australia state.
Police had expressed grave concern for their safety shortly before the first six were found by police within 15 km of Norseman after a trek of 60 km.
The woman, 27-year-old Wanda Schultz, and the rest of the children were found about 30 minutes later.
"They all seem fine and quite happy," a hospital spokeswoman told reporters.

Schultz and the children, aged between seven months and 16 years, had crammed into a small station wagon when they set out in search of bardy grubs, a traditional Aboriginal food. The car later broke down.
The six had followed a highway leading to Norseman for two days, police said. They were led by an unidentified 16-year-old.
"While they followed the highway they didn't actually walk on it," a police spokesman told reporters.
"They meandered through the scrub. Perhaps they thought they had done something wrong... They got so close to making it back on foot," he said.
Schultz and the remaining seven children had stayed with the vehicle in lightly wooded countryside, police said.
Emergency services and police launched a search over an area of up to 7,000 sq km (2,700 square miles) when the group failed to return on Saturday.
All but one of the children are Aboriginal. Schultz is the mother of five of the children, with the rest belonging to relatives and friends, police said.
